title: How many factors does thirty six have, and why is the count odd?
description: The video counts the factors of thirty six by writing them in pairs, and finds why the count turns out odd. Keeko doubts the count after treating every pair as two separate factors.
teaching_notes: One idea: factors come in pairs, except when a number is paired with itself. The pair six and six gives only one factor, so the count is odd. Watch for students who count both numbers of the last pair and get an even total.

source: Count the factors of 36 and say why the count is odd.
video_script.why: The child sees that factors of a number pair up, and that only a number paired with itself makes the count odd.
video_script.substitution: Write every factor pair of the number, then count the factors, counting a repeated factor once.
video_script.anchor: the row of lockers of Ruhee with locker 36 marked
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees five pairs and counts two factors for each pair, so says ten factors. In the last pair six and six are the same number, so it counts only once.
video_script.payoff_line: Thirty six has nine factors, because six pairs with itself

final_answer.spoken: nine factors, and the odd count comes from six times six

names.Ruhee: the queen of Khoisnam whose will hides the treasure in one of 100 lockers

never_show: the idea that the open lockers are the square numbers
maths_rules: five pairs, but 6 × 6 uses the same number twice, so 4 pairs × 2 + 1 = 9
the slip: 5 pairs × 2 = 10, which counts 6 twice
video_script.design: One idea: pairs of factors, with one pair that has the same number twice. Wrong idea: counting both numbers of every pair. The pair board stays on the stage.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Thirty six has nine factors, because six pairs with itself.
Four pairs give eight factors, and the single six makes the count odd.

<bookmark mark='fix'/>A factor is counted once, so that pair adds one, not two.
